section_summary: This section contains FBI-translated transcripts of Japanese short-wave broadcasts from September 3–9, 1941, with covering letters to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle Jr. The broadcasts report on the war in China, the German–Soviet war, the USS Greer incident, and Japanese relations with the United States and French Indochina; their commentaries promote Japan’s wartime policies. The section ends with an embassy despatch enclosing an October 1941 Radio Tokyo programme booklet.

subfiles.title: Continuation of translated Japanese broadcast
subfiles.about: A broadcast commentary discusses Japan’s policies and the wars in China and Europe.
subfiles.summary: Continued commentary defends Japan’s actions in China and describes its stated aim of preserving peace in East Asia.

subfiles.title: FBI letter enclosing September 3–4 Tokyo broadcast transcripts
subfiles.about: The FBI sends translated Tokyo broadcasts for September 3 and 4, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter transmitting two translated broadcast transcripts.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 3, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast combines war news with commentary on French Indochina and Japanese national service.
subfiles.summary: News reports Japanese raids in China, the German–Soviet war, and Japanese–American diplomacy. Commentary promotes Japanese influence in French Indochina. A longer talk by Furuyasu Irizawa describes cooperative living, food production, material conservation, and national mobilisation in Japan.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 4, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports war developments and presents extended arguments about the ABCD encirclement and Japanese–American relations.
subfiles.summary: News covers the Japanese evacuation of Fuzhou, events in China and Europe, and U.S. aid to other countries. A commentary repeats Mabuchi’s warning that Japan may use force against the ABCD encirclement and links that stance to air raids on Chongqing. Zenzo Naoni’s talk argues that U.S. economic pressure threatens Japan while discussing Konoe’s message to Roosevelt.

subfiles.title: FBI letter enclosing September 5–9 Tokyo broadcast transcripts
subfiles.about: The FBI sends translated Tokyo broadcasts for September 5–9, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter transmitting five days of broadcast transcripts.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 5, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports Japanese government and military news, the USS Greer incident, and economic preparations.
subfiles.summary: News includes cabinet measures, fighting in China, French Indochina, the German–Soviet war, and the USS Greer. A closing commentary claims Japan is building East Asian economic self-sufficiency against British and American restrictions.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 6, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast covers the Greer dispute, war news, British shipping, and Japan’s troop deployment in French Indochina.
subfiles.summary: News reports the Greer dispute and German operations against the Soviet Union. A commentary predicts that shipping losses will weaken Britain; a children’s segment praises Japan’s readiness. Major Shozo Falkajira then describes the Japanese landing in southern French Indochina and presents it as defensive.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 7, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast presents competing claims about the USS Greer and reports on fighting in China and Europe.
subfiles.summary: Much of the news concerns German and American accounts of the Greer incident. Other items address Japanese raids in China, the siege of Leningrad, and Iran. A commentary portrays U.S. support for Chongqing as ineffective against Japan’s blockade.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 8, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast covers the Greer incident, Roosevelt’s postponed speech, war reports, and Japanese domestic news.
subfiles.summary: News follows the Greer dispute, reports Sara Roosevelt’s death, and covers Japanese economic and military matters alongside European war developments. A weekly review recalls recent Japanese measures; a short talk describes an example of cooperation among travellers.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme, September 9, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast announces a Japanese envoy to French Indochina and reports on the Greer incident and wider war.
subfiles.summary: News announces Kenkichi Yoshizawa’s appointment and continued Japanese claims about the Greer incident. It also reports fighting in China and Europe, developments in Iran, and Manchukuo’s economic plan. The programme closes with children’s compositions.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch enclosing Radio Tokyo programmes for October 1941
subfiles.from: Frank S. Williams, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards nine copies of Radio Tokyo’s October 1941 programme booklet.
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding October programme copies and suggesting their distribution.

subfiles.title: Radio Tokyo, No. 63: October 1941 programme
subfiles.about: The booklet advertises Radio Tokyo short-wave programmes and transmission schedules.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages introduce worldwide short-wave service, list October programme highlights and contributors, and give frequencies and times for Southwestern Asia and the Near East. The schedule continues beyond this section.
